arxiv-2103-17271.title: DCVNet: Dilated Cost Volume Networks for Fast Optical Flow
arxiv-2103-17271.creator: Huaizu Jiang, Erik Learned-Miller
arxiv-2103-17271.description: Abstract The cost volume, capturing the similarity of possible correspondences across two input images, is a key ingredient in state-of-the-art optical flow approaches. When sampling correspondences to build the cost volume, a large neighborhood radius is required to deal with large displacements, introducing a significant computational burden.

arxiv-2110-03616.title: Cyclotomic expansion for the colored HOMFLY-PT invariants of double twist knots
arxiv-2110-03616.creator: Qingtao Chen, Kefeng Liu and Shengmao Zhu
arxiv-2110-03616.description: Abstract . In this short note, we prove the cyclotomic expansion formula for the colored HOMFLY-PT invariant of double twist knots, it confirms the cyclotomic expansion conjecture for S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) -invariants proposed in [ 2 ] . 1.

arxiv-2210-15630.title: In-stream Probabilistic Cardinality Estimation for Bloom Filters
arxiv-2210-15630.creator: Rémy Scholler, Jean-François Couchot, Oumaïma Alaoui-Ismaïli, Denis Renaud, Eric Ballot
arxiv-2210-15630.description: Abstract The amount of data coming from different sources such as IoT-sensors, social networks, cellular networks, has increased exponentially during the last few years. Probabilistic Data Structures (PDS) are efficient alternatives to deterministic data structures suitable for large data processing and streaming applications. They are mainly used for approximate membership queries, frequency count, cardinality estimation and similarity research.

arxiv-2301-05768.title: RxRx1: A Dataset for Evaluating Experimental Batch Correction Methods
arxiv-2301-05768.creator: Maciej Sypetkowski, Morteza Rezanejad, Saber Saberian, Oren Kraus, John Urbanik, James Taylor, Ben Mabey, Mason Victors, Jason Yosinski, Alborz Rezazadeh Sereshkeh, Imran Haque, Berton Earnshaw
arxiv-2301-05768.description: Abstract High-throughput screening techniques are commonly used to obtain large quantities of data in many fields of biology. It is well known that artifacts arising from variability in the technical execution of different experimental batches within such screens confound these observations and can lead to invalid biological conclusions.

arxiv-2302-06915.title: Formation of trapped surfaces in the Einstein-Yang-Mills system
arxiv-2302-06915.creator: Nikolaos Athanasiou, Puskar Mondal, Shing-Tung Yau
arxiv-2302-06915.description: Abstract We prove a scale-invariant, semi-global existence result and a trapped surface formation result in the context of coupled Einstein-Yang-Mills theory, without symmetry assumptions. More precisely, we prove a scale-invariant semi-global existence theorem from past null-infinity and show that the focusing of the gravitational and/or chromoelectric-chromomagnetic waves could lead to the formation of a trapped surface.

arxiv-2311-02151.title: Vanishing performance of the parity-encoded quantum approximate optimization algorithm applied to spin-glass models
arxiv-2311-02151.creator: Elisabeth Wybo, Martin Leib
arxiv-2311-02151.description: Abstract The parity mapping provides a geometrically local encoding of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), at the expense of having a quadratic qubit overhead for all-to-all connected problems. In this work, we benchmark the parity-encoded QAOA on spin-glass models. We address open questions in the scaling of this algorithm.

arxiv-2408-06837.title: How Aligned are Human Chart Takeaways and LLM Predictions? A Case Study on Bar Charts with Varying Layouts
arxiv-2408-06837.creator: Huichen Will Wang, Jane Hoffswell, Sao Myat Thazin Thane, Victor S. Bursztyn, and Cindy Xiong Bearfield
arxiv-2408-06837.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have been adopted for a variety of visualizations tasks, but how far are we from perceptually aware LLMs that can predict human takeaways? Graphical perception literature has shown that human chart takeaways are sensitive to visualization design choices, such as spatial layouts.

arxiv-2507-22033.title: On the formation of strange quark stars from supernova in compact binaries Journal: Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
arxiv-2507-22033.creator: L. M. Becerra, F. Cipolletta, A. Drago, M. Guerrini, A. Lavagno, G. Pagliara, J. A. Rueda
arxiv-2507-22033.description: Abstract Strange quark stars (SQSs), namely compact stars entirely composed of deconfined quark matter, are characterized by similar masses and compactness to neutron stars (NSs) and have been theoretically proposed to exist in the Universe since the 1970s. However, multiwavelength observations of compact stars in the last 50 years have not yet led to an unambiguous SQS identification.

arxiv-2509-09322.title: ORCA: Unveiling Obscure Containers In The Wild
arxiv-2509-09322.creator: Jacopo Bufalino, Agathe Blaise, Stefano Secci
arxiv-2509-09322.description: Abstract . Modern software development increasingly depends on open-source libraries and third-party components, which are often encapsulated into containerized environments. While improving the development and deployment of applications, this approach introduces security risks, particularly when outdated or vulnerable components are inadvertently included in production environments.

pmc-12692065.title: Age-Related Changes in Neuron–Microglia Interaction Mediated by Fractalkine Under Inflammatory Conditions
pmc-12692065.creator: Rommy von Bernhardi, Franchesca Cortes, Claudia Narea, Claudia Metz, Gaston Godoy, Jaime Eugenin
pmc-12692065.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Ageing results in an increased microglial activation and neuroinflammation. We are interested in assessing ageing-dependent changes in the amount and fractalkine (CX3CL1) proteoforms participating in neuron–microglia crosstalk that could be involved in microglia activation. We analysed age-dependent changes in CX3CL1, CX3CR1, and TGFβ mRNAs using RT-qPCR and CX3CL1 proteoforms using Western blot, in 3 to 20-month-old WT mice and an inflammatory mouse model (SRA−/−) treated with 0.5 mg/kg of intraperitoneal LPS, 2 ng of intrathecal TGFβ, or a vehicle.

pmc-13045246.title: rTPI : An R Package for Calculating Thermal and Aridity Position Indices for Terrestrial Vertebrates
pmc-13045246.creator: Matthew J Watson, Jeremy T Kerr
pmc-13045246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Species environmental niche limits provide useful information for generating estimates of species niche position. Recent work investigating species' responses to climate change has shown that models that included metrics of species‐specific thermal and aridity niche position improve in performance. However, availability to generate thermal and aridity niche limits as well as estimates of niche position has been lacking for large numbers of species.

pmc-13069802.title: Basilar artery flow velocities and optic nerve sheath diameter as adjuvant tools for early diagnosis of hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy in neonates
pmc-13069802.creator: Marwa Mohamed Farag, Mohamed Alaa Eldin Hassan Thabet, Islam SH Ahmed, Husam Mohamed Abu Halawa
pmc-13069802.description: ObjectiveWe investigated potentiality ultrasonography measured optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) and basilar artery (BA) velocities to identify neonates with HIE-requiring-TH.MethodsStudy was of a case-control-design. Thirty- five neonates with mild-to-severe HIE admitted to NICU of Alexandria-University-Maternity-Hospital and were monitored by ultrasound-measured ONSD and BA velocities, in first-12-hours, during TH, and after rewarming. First scan measures of patients were compared to healthy-control-neonates.

pmc-13089909.title: Effect of Polymer Structure on the Thermodynamics of Polyelectrolyte Complex Micelle Formation
pmc-13089909.creator: Vishnu L. Dharmaraj, Yun Fang, Matthew V. Tirrell
pmc-13089909.description: Polyelectrolyte complex micelles (PCMs) are nanoparticles that form through the associative phase separation between hydrophilic neutral–charged block copolymers and oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, resulting in a dense, charged core surrounded by a stabilizing neutral corona. Among other applications, these constructs have been studied as nonviral vectors for therapeutic nucleic acid delivery for a variety of potential clinical indications.

pmc-13354748.title: Choledochal Villous Adenoma With Intrahepatic Bile Duct Stones: A Case Report
pmc-13354748.creator: Hao Li, Shaohua Sun, Wenbo Zhou
pmc-13354748.description: This report describes a 58‐year‐old female with prior biliary surgery who presented with a choledochal villous adenoma and intrahepatic stones. The lesion showed high‐grade intraepithelial neoplasia, indicating malignant potential. She underwent left hemihepatectomy, choledochectomy, and Roux‐en‐Y hepaticojejunostomy, with no recurrence at 4‐month follow‐up.

pmc-13369476.title: Pivoting forestry and agricultural concessions toward conservation in Southeast Asia
pmc-13369476.creator: Annabel Jia Yi Lim, Yiwen Zeng, Hoong Chen Teo, Jose Don T De Alban, Lian Pin Koh
pmc-13369476.description: Expansion of forestry and agriculture in Southeast Asia has driven widespread deforestation, biodiversity loss and carbon emissions. Yet large areas of natural forest remain within concessions, representing overlooked opportunities for conservation and climate mitigation. We identify 42 Mha of natural tropical moist forest within 3,754 logging, oil palm, planted wood and rubber concessions across Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and Myanmar.
